brief.desc: Gold closed the week with modest gains as a softening US dollar and persistent sovereign accumulation provided solid underlying support. While elevated bond yields continue to generate friction, safe-haven hedging and sustained Chinese physical demand are keeping buyers active on pullbacks.
brief.yr: During the Friday, September 25, 2026 session, the SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) gained +0.44% (+$1.72) to close at $393.41, rebounding off an intraday low of $390.05 to reach a session peak of $394.22. Gold caught a steady bid as the US Dollar index pulled back from recent highs, giving bullion room to recover despite persistent headwinds from elevated bond yields. Support was reinforced by robust long-term demand fundamentals, highlighted by heavy sovereign and physical accumulation in Asia. Strong institutional interest helped the metal close the week on positive footing near session highs.
brief.to: Heading into Monday, September 28, 2026, gold's near-term direction will hinge on the US dollar's trajectory and Treasury yield movements alongside incoming central bank commentary. Immediate upside resistance for GLD stands at Friday's high of $394.22, with a breakout paving the way for a test of psychological resistance toward $398.00. Downside support is anchored at Friday's low of $390.05, followed by critical base support near the $385.00 handle, which should attract dip-buyers if selling pressure re-emerges.
